# Golden QR Code matrices for internal/approval/qr: byte mode, error
# correction level M, versions 1-10. Invented payloads, no secrets.
#
# Generated offline on 2026-10-16 by an established encoder: Project Nayuki's
# "QR Code generator library", Python package qrcodegen 1.8.0 (wheel sha256
# 06bf87021bc351f1c6e722ac67db8a059c4fe27bbfbca39ed7a9a2364abdd7a6), run in
# python:3.14-slim, with
#   QrCode.encode_segments([QrSegment.make_bytes(payload)],
#                          QrCode.Ecc.MEDIUM, 1, 10, mask, False)
# where mask is -1 for "mask auto" (the encoder's own penalty scoring picks
# it) and boostecl False keeps level M.
#
# Cross-checked against a second encoder, segno 1.6.6 (wheel sha256
# 28c7d081ed0cf935e0411293a465efd4d500704072cdb039778a2ab8736190c7): for
# full-capacity payloads (versions 1-10, every mask) the two agree module for
# module. For payloads with spare capacity segno differs, because it appends
# eight zero padding bits even when the bit stream already ends on a codeword
# boundary (ISO/IEC 18004 7.4.10 adds padding bits only when it does not).
#
# Format: everything before the first "case" line is this header. Each case is
#   case <id>
#   payload hex:<payload bytes in hex> | uri:<name>
#   mask auto | <0-7>
#   version <1-10>
#   chosen <mask the encoder used>
#   <one line per row, '#' dark and '.' light, no quiet zone>
#   end
# "uri:<name>" is the otpauth URI for <name> with the RFC 6238 Appendix B
# SHA-1 test seed ("12345678901234567890"), which the test builds itself.

case empty
payload hex:
mask auto
version 1
chosen 3
